whatItDoes: A Node CLI (second-copy.mjs), with a browser page that runs the same module on the same snapshots, reads three things from PartForge: the flight doctrine (the flightSystemPrompt() slice that tests/run.mjs takes), the GRADE_SY literal with its comment, and the seven flight templates. It pairs each number it can with the table key and column next to it and judges it against data/tables/*.json at the literal's own printed precision. Verdicts are AGREES, DISAGREES, UNBACKED, NON-CLASS, MAPPED or QUOTED, and a line-by-line COPY-DRIFT check compares tests/templates/*.scad with the copies index.html ships. At 0974a62 the result is 8 DISAGREES, 1 COPY-DRIFT, 11 NON-CLASS, 18 UNBACKED, 1 MAPPED, 1 QUOTED and 125 AGREES (exit 1). Replaying the doctrine's fastener, fit and O-ring bullets at ad4d587 and 3bffbe0 flags 15 of the 16 UN clearances, and exactly the six mis-filed Parker widths that orings_as568.json's own project_issues lists.

findingsAboutSourceRepo:
PartForge at 0974a62. Observed only; nothing was fixed there.

- **F1.** The bulkhead orders the wrong O-ring.
  - tests/templates/bulkhead.scad:6 (shipped copy at index.html:2057) says "AS568-250, ID 4.984 in = 126.59 mm, W 0.103 in = 2.62 mm".
  - orings_as568.json makes -250 a W 0.139 in (3.53 mm) ring. The W .103 dash at that ID is -159 (ID 4.987).
  - The groove at bulkhead.scad:56–58 is cut for W .103; :55 repeats "AS568-250".
  - A -250 ring's section is 9.79 mm² against a 6.08 mm² groove.
- **F2.** bulkhead.scad:7 (index.html:2058) gives the Chart 4-3 liquids width as ".140-.146"; the chart says .136–.142 in.
  - .140–.146 in is the old mis-filed band that orings project_issues[2] names.
  - The doctrine was fixed at fae75b8; this template line was not, although project_issues[5] names the bulkhead template.
- **F3.** The nosecone names H7 for its Ø20 pocket but declares ±0.05.
  - nosecone.scad:3, :7 and :43; FLIGHT bore at :21.
  - H7 at Ø20 is 20.000–20.021.
- **F4.** The doctrine's own FLIGHT example (index.html:1440) declares coupler OD 149.300 ±0.05 and cites "ISO 286 H7/g6 at 120-180 mm"; g6 is 149.261–149.286.
- **F5.** index.html:1454 says "four vendors' 6 in airframes share ID 152.4 mm". In airframes.json three do; PML is 152.578, as flight-db.test.mjs:34 itself asserts.
- **F6.** The template copies have drifted.
  - bulkhead.scad:11 differs from index.html:2062 and has since 9e79f4c (2026-09-18). At that commit the shipped copy still said "SF > 3 on a grade-2 steel U-bolt"; ebde615 later reworded it.
  - docs/STATUS.md:19 claims every template is byte-identical to the shipped copy.
  - The drift test that backs that claim (tests/flight-decl.test.mjs:163–182) compares only the "loads" line.
- **F7.** The doctrine restates 25 fastener numbers that the comment at flight-db.test.mjs:61 forbids: 23 metric values at index.html:1493, plus 6.75 and 7.14 in its own parenthesis. All agree today and none is pinned. The regex at :66 guards only four strings.
- **F8.** index.html:1494 gives p6 zones at three sizes.
  - fits.json carries no p letter; its notes, LIMITS (2), withhold interference letters.
  - flight-db.test.mjs:137 asserts that the reference hint refuses p6.
  - The p6 widths equal IT6; the deviations are unbacked.
- **F9.** "Light press" has two copies: index.html:1494 calls k6 the light press, while :1454 and fits.json's named fits call H7/n6 the light press and H7/k6 a transition fit. I read this by hand.
- **F10.** The doctrine's typical MMT sizes at index.html:1507 (98.5, 75.4, 54.4 ID) match no body tube in airframes.json. They are marked "≈", so reported as UNBACKED.
- **F11.** GRADE_SY (index.html:5804) uses 640 MPa for 8.8 at every size; the table's note gives 660 above M16. This is conservative, so not a defect.
- **F12.** Four templates assume an airframe the table does not carry.
  - centering-ring, coupler, motor-retainer and nosecone (line 4 in each) assume airframe ID 149.60 mm. No body tube in airframes.json is within 0.6 mm of that.
  - fin.scad:6 assumes ID 148.4 for the same 152.40 mm OD.
  - I read this by hand from the full table.
- **Stale citations in the proposal:**
  - The flight-db guard is :57–69, with the regex at :66.
  - The fits line is :1494 and the O-ring line :1495, not ≈1495–1496.
  - The roadmap-evaluation's GRADE_SY :4929 is stale; it is now :5804.
deviationsFromProposal:
- **Tolerance.** The proposal declared 0.0005 mm / 0.5 µm. I use "equal at the literal's printed precision (±½ unit in its last digit)", with UN, AS568 and Parker values compared from the inch columns × 25.4. The proposal's rule calls every correctly rounded inch conversion a disagreement, including the doctrine's own 6.75 for 6.746875; as a sabotage it fails 18 of the 32 tests. UN clearances also agree with ASME B18.2.8's printed nominal, which the table carries.
- **More families than proposed:**
  - NASA design factors, the motor_perf row count (1037) and the 11.6 kN example
  - motor case diameters, the "four vendors" airframe claim and the MMT typicals
  - AS568 dash rows and the Parker ±.003 attribution
  - GRADE_SY's comment as a second copy, and the doctrine's grade names against GRADE_SY's keys
  - all from airframes, motors and design_factors_nasa excerpts, so that "every" holds where a resolver exists.
- **New verdicts and an inventory.**
  - COPY-DRIFT generalises PartForge's loads-line sync test.
  - QUOTED keeps the doctrine's own sentence about its past 6.76 error from being judged.
  - MAPPED gives "a4-80 by assumption" its own verdict.
  - The unpaired-number inventory makes coverage visible: 119 of the doctrine's 272 numbers are claimed.
- **Pairing method.** The proposal tokenised within a short window. I use explicit sentence shapes instead: on the real text, window pairing mis-pairs "M6 class 8.8 … clearance 6.40" and a hole size with its reason, and the gland lists are positional.
- **History replays** were not in the proposal. They keep only the doctrine's three table bullets at each commit, to stay under budget.
- **A browser page and a `--brief` mode** were added to the CLI proposal.
- **Planted fixtures** are built in memory from the snapshots rather than stored as files; the GRADE_SY 660 fixture becomes a temporary file in the CLI test.
- **18-8** stays UNBACKED and **a4-80** MAPPED, as the proposal's test plan said.
- **Snapshot layout.** One snapshot per source file. The shipped bulkhead copy is stored as one replaced line on its tests/templates twin plus a sha256 that is verified on rebuild. This keeps `du -sk` at 496 KB.
notBuilt:
- **Not wired into PartForge.** Nothing is wired into tests/run.mjs or tools/db. I did not run PartForge's own test suite, because it writes tests/.build inside the checkout.
- **Resolvers are fitted to sentence shapes.** They cover the shapes used by the doctrine and the seven shipped templates. Model-written NOTE lines in other forms are not paired; they are only counted as unpaired.
- **The unpaired inventory is heuristic.** It depends on an identifier mask that decides what counts as a number.
- **Two findings come from reading, not from the tool.** The light-press labels (F9) and the templates' airframe ID assumption (F12) were read by hand; no resolver covers them.
- **History replays are partial.** They use only the doctrine's three table bullets and compare them with today's tables. 3bffbe0 predates the tables, so that replay is backed only by the agreement with project_issues.
- **No external check of the values themselves:**
  - The a4-80 → A2-80 equivalence is from memory and not verified against ISO 3506-1.
  - Whether p6 at +35/+22 µm, the SAE J429 strengths (393/634/896) and 18-8 at 450 are correct is not established. No table carries them, and nothing was retyped from memory.
- **No maintainer has confirmed any finding**, and the deposit has not been through PartForge's data-provenance pipeline, geometry gate or skeptic review.
- **The page skips one hash check.** It rebuilds the shipped templates without checking their sha256 (it does no hashing). The CLI and the tests do check it.
- **Other changes in the bank are not mine.** The bank repository's git status shows changes in sibling folders (for example, a deleted ideas/05-round-trip-ledger/example.svg) that belong to other builders. I wrote only inside ideas/18-second-copy; PartForge, Skyhook, Aster and Idea-Bank are clean.
